events.title: JavaScript prototyped at Netscape
events.summary: Brendan Eich built the first Mocha prototype in ten days in May 1995 for scriptable web pages in Netscape Navigator.
events.about: JavaScript runs inside the web browser to make pages interactive — validate a form before submit, swap menu tabs, fetch data without reloading. Today it also powers servers (Node.js), mobile apps (React Native), and most front-end frameworks. In 1995 it was mainly: buttons, alerts, and simple page behavior.

narrative.whyChosen: This hack became the language of the browser and eventually one of the most used languages on Earth.
narrative.whyImportant: It made web pages reactive without Java applets or server round-trips for every interaction.
narrative.problemSolved: HTML alone could not respond to users; Netscape needed an embeddable scripting language fast.

events.title: Java announced at SunWorld
events.summary: Sun Microsystems and Netscape announced Java as a portable language for the web, paired with Navigator integration.
events.about: Java promised "write once, run anywhere" via the JVM — same bytecode on Windows, Mac, or Unix. In the 1990s it was famous for browser applets (animations, calculators in web pages) and quickly became the default for enterprise backends, Android apps, and large server systems.

narrative.whyChosen: Java's 'write once, run anywhere' promise reshaped enterprise software and mobile (via Android later).
narrative.whyImportant: It made the JVM model mainstream and pushed garbage-collected OOP into mainstream industry use.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers faced fragmented native platforms; Java targeted bytecode portability and sandboxed applets.

sources.title: Sun — Java Technology: The Early Years (May 23, 1995)

events.title: MySQL first released
events.summary: Michael Widenius and MySQL AB shipped the first MySQL release on May 23, 1995 — a fast SQL database with an mSQL-compatible API.
events.about: MySQL powers LAMP stacks, WordPress, early Facebook, and countless web apps needing a simple relational store. Teams run `SELECT`, `JOIN`, and transactions for CRUD APIs and reporting. It became the default cheap SQL option before PostgreSQL's rise and cloud-managed databases.

narrative.whyChosen: MySQL made SQL databases accessible to every PHP and web hosting provider on the planet.
narrative.whyImportant: Its speed and simple licensing defined the open-source database market for a decade.
narrative.problemSolved: mSQL was too slow and closed; developers needed a fast SQL engine with a familiar API.

sources.title: MySQL — History of MySQL (first version May 23, 1995)

events.title: Bill Gates declares the "Internet tidal wave"
events.quoteText: The Internet is a tidal wave. It changes the rules. It is an incredible opportunity as well as an incredible challenge.
events.summary: Bill Gates's internal Microsoft memo redirects the company to make the Internet central to every product.
events.about: Gates had initially dismissed the web; this memo is the pivot. It led to IE bundling, MSN strategy, and the browser wars — and later antitrust scrutiny.

narrative.whyChosen: The moment Microsoft officially bet the company on the web.
narrative.whyImportant: It accelerated browser development and reshaped Windows as a networked platform.
narrative.problemSolved: Microsoft risked missing the Internet after focusing on desktop CD-ROM products.
